standard.title: Mathematical Modelling with Percentages
standard.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts; formulate problems, choosing efficient calculation strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, reviewing the appropriateness of the model
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can model practical problems with rational numbers and percentages (from AC9M7N09). Students can apply four operations to integers and rationals (from AC9M8N04).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students formulate and solve practical models involving percentage increase/decrease, financial contexts including tax, and problems with negative quantities; review model appropriateness and communicate solutions.

nodes.label: Modelling percentage increase and decrease
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students model situations involving percentage increase and decrease, including mark-ups, discounts, and GST, and explain why the result is an increase or decrease.
nodes.minimum_width: Model a percentage increase or decrease problem (e.g. discount, mark-up) and explain why the result is higher or lower.
nodes.typical_width: Apply percentage modelling to mark-ups, discounts, GST, and market trends; explain the direction of change; use multiplier approach for efficiency.
wider: Investigate successive percentage changes — why does a 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease not return to the original? Develop a general model.
Model environmental or population contexts involving percentage change over extended time periods — connect to exponential growth informally.

response_modes.reason: Percentage increase and decrease problems span a wide range of structures and contexts. Students who only practise one type (e.g. discount) fail to recognise the same structure in other contexts (e.g. tax, population change).

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 financial modelling includes percentage-based tax and interest calculations — students who cannot reliably apply percentage increase/decrease across varied contexts cannot set up the financial models that depend on this reasoning.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Successive percentage changes and the non-commutativity of percentage operations are rich structural insights for advancing students — connecting to exponential growth is a meaningful conceptual extension within Year 8.
success_criteria: Correctly models a percentage increase or decrease problem.
Explains why the change is an increase or decrease.
Uses an efficient multiplier strategy where appropriate.

nodes.label: Modelling financial and real-world contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students formulate and solve models for financial problems including personal income tax, and interpret and communicate solutions including review of model appropriateness.
nodes.minimum_width: Model a simple financial problem (e.g. tax bracket, pay rate) and interpret the solution in context.
nodes.typical_width: Apply modelling to income tax, comparing taxation brackets; model weather/environmental contexts with positive and negative quantities; review whether the model is appropriate for the situation.
wider: Model personal income tax across multiple tax brackets — calculate effective tax rate and compare to marginal rate.
Investigate modelling of sea depth or temperature changes using negative quantities — apply to real environmental data.

response_modes.reason: Financial modelling requires simultaneous application of percentage operations, negative number handling, and communication of results in context — the integration of all prior number strand work at Year 8.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Income tax bracket modelling with effective vs marginal rate comparison is a rich and practically significant application for advancing students that connects all rational number operations in a meaningful real-world context.
success_criteria: Formulates a model correctly from a financial or real-world context.
Interprets the solution with appropriate units and contextual meaning.
Reviews whether the model captures the situation accurately.
